name: 02-tailwind-v3-id-trap
guards: The Tailwind v3-vs-v4 Context7 id. sources.yaml lists two ids for one domain: /websites/tailwindcss is v4, /websites/v3_tailwindcss is v3. Querying the wrong one returns fluent, wrong answers — v4 is CSS-first (@theme, @import "tailwindcss"), v3 is JS-config, and v4 syntax in a v3 project silently produces unstyled output. sources.yaml also records Tailwind's llms.txt as a confirmed 404, so probing tier 2 here is re-discovering a known absence.
query: Add a custom brand colour (#0f5132) and a custom '2xs' font size to this project's Tailwind setup. Show me exactly where they go and what the config should look like.
expected_behavior: The context-brief skill loads and runs (the runner invokes it explicitly by default, so this checks that it loads — not that it auto-triggers; use --auto-trigger to test triggering)
Identifies the installed Tailwind major as 3.x from the project's own files before choosing a source
Queries the v3 Context7 id (/websites/v3_tailwindcss) and not the v4 id (/websites/tailwindcss)
Does not fetch or probe a Tailwind llms.txt — sources.yaml records it as a confirmed 404 with an llms_txt_checked date

Answers in v3 JS-config syntax (theme.extend in tailwind.config.js) and prescribes no v4 CSS-first syntax such as @theme or @import "tailwindcss". Scoped to code blocks: naming v4 syntax in prose to warn against it is correct behaviour, not a failure.
